extraction.name: MATH
extraction.description: A dataset of 12,500 challenging competition mathematics problems (7,500 training and 5,000 test) from competitions including AMC 10, AMC 12, and AIME. Each problem includes a full step-by-step solution and a final boxed answer, tagged by difficulty (1-5) and spanning seven subjects including Prealgebra, Algebra, Number Theory, Counting and Probability, Geometry, Intermediate Algebra, and Precalculus.
extraction.creator: Dan Hendrycks, Collin Burns, Saurav Kadavath, Akul Arora, Steven Basart, Eric Tang, Dawn Song, Jacob Steinhardt
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The MATH dataset consists of 12,500 problems from high school math competitions, tagged by difficulty (1-5) and spanning seven subjects. The AMPS pretraining dataset consists of problems generated with Mathematica and Khan Academy exercise framework code.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: High school math competition problems from the Mathematical Association of America (MAA), problems generated with Mathematica, and Khan Academy exercise modules covering a wide range of mathematical topics.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human evaluation on a sample of 20 problems from the MATH test set; participants had 1 hour and performed calculations by hand
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: University students with varying mathematical backgrounds, including one who does not like mathematics, one ambivalent toward mathematics, two who like mathematics, one who got a perfect score on the AMC 10 and attended USAMO, and a three-time IMO gold medalist
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Automatic answer assessment using exact match with formatting normalization rules and the \boxed{} delimiter
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The MATH dataset is limited to competition-level mathematics problems, and model accuracy is slowly increasing, suggesting that conceptual and algorithmic breakthroughs are needed for strong performance.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Solving the MATH dataset with machine learning would have broad practical and intellectual significance given the wide applicability of mathematics.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The MATH benchmark is intended for measuring mathematical problem-solving ability, and AMPS is a pretraining corpus for enabling models to learn K-12 mathematics. Both support training, fine-tuning, and evaluation of ML models.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Khan Academy data is upsampled by a factor of 5 and Mathematica data is downsampled by a factor of 2 during pretraining to account for the large difference in dataset sizes.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Models are fine-tuned with an equal mix of final answer sequences and full solution sequences. GPT-2 tokenizes numbers digit by digit. T5's tokenizer was found to remove many LaTeX symbols and was not used.

name.evidence: we introduce MATH, a new dataset of 12,500 challenging competition mathematics problems

description.evidence: The Mathematics Aptitude Test of Heuristics dataset, abbreviated MATH, has 12,500 problems (7,500 training and 5,000 test). With this many training problems, models can learn many useful heuristics for problem solving. Each problem has a step-by-step solution and a final boxed answer.

creator.evidence: Dan Hendrycks UC Berkeley, Collin Burns UC Berkeley, Saurav Kadavath UC Berkeley, Akul Arora UC Berkeley, Steven Basart UChicago, Eric Tang UC Berkeley, Dawn Song UC Berkeley, Jacob Steinhardt UC Berkeley

inLanguage.evidence: Problems and solutions are consistently formatted using LaTeX and the Asymptote vector graphics language.

isLiveDataset.evidence: The Mathematics Aptitude Test of Heuristics dataset, abbreviated MATH, has 12,500 problems (7,500 training and 5,000 test).

rai:dataCollection.evidence: we introduce the MATH dataset, which consists of 12, 500 problems from high school math competitions... AMPS consists of problems generated with Mathematica and Khan Academy code.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: MATH problems are created by the Mathematical Association of America (MAA)... AMPS consists of problems generated with Mathematica and Khan Academy code. Khan Academy's exercise framework follows an MIT License.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: MATH problems are created by the Mathematical Association of America (MAA)... AMPS consists of problems generated with Mathematica and Khan Academy code.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: we randomly sampled 20 problems from the MATH test set and gave them to humans. We artificially require that the participants have 1 hour to work on the problems and must perform calculations by hand.

rai:annotatorDemographics.evidence: All participants are university students. One participant who does not like mathematics got 8/20 = 40% correct. A participant ambivalent toward mathematics got 13/20. Two participants who like mathematics got 14/20 and 15/20. A participant who got a perfect score on the AMC 10 exam and attended USAMO several times got 18/20. A three-time IMO gold medalist got 18/20 = 90%

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: Due to design choices in MATH, we can assess the answers generated by a model automatically, even though the space of model outputs is combinatorially large. Automatic assessment starts by determining the beginning and end of the answer... by parsing what is inside the \boxed{} command and comparing that with the ground truth answer

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: We showed that accuracy is slowly increasing and, if trends continue, the community will need to discover conceptual and algorithmic breakthroughs to attain strong performance on MATH.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: Given the broad reach and applicability of mathematics, solving the MATH dataset with machine learning would be of profound practical and intellectual signiﬁcance.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: We introduced the MATH benchmark, which enables the community to measure mathematical problem-solving ability... We also introduce AMPS, a diverse pretraining corpus that can enable future models to learn virtually all of K-12 mathematics.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: During pretraining, we upsample Khan Academy data by a factor of 5 and we downsample Mathematica by a factor of 2 to account for the large difference in dataset sizes.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: we train with an equal mix of '⟨P⟩Final Answer: <Answer>' and '⟨P⟩Full Solution: <Step-by-Step Solution>' sequences... Our GPT-2 models tokenizes numbers so that one digit is processed at a time... T5's tokenizer removes many LATEX symbols
